sections.h2: Where is Grady County and which towns sit inside it?
sections.html:
Grady County lies along Georgia's southern border with Florida. Cairo is both the county seat and the largest city. The county dates from August 17, 1905, when the General Assembly cut it from parts of Decatur and Thomas; its namesake is Henry W. Grady, an orator and editor of the Atlanta Constitution (Wikipedia).

The county spans 460 square miles, 455 of them land. Water here mostly flows into the Ochlockonee River, with the northwest corner draining toward the Flint, and the Red Hills Region extends into the county. Its neighbors are Mitchell to the north, Thomas to the east and Decatur to the west, with the Florida counties of Leon and Gadsden along the south.

Cairo and Whigham are the only incorporated cities. Calvary is classed by the Census Bureau as a place, and Beachton and Spence are crossroads outside any city limits. Grady County Schools operates six public schools, including Cairo High School. Every parcel appears on one county digest, and cities can add their own levy, which makes each line of the bill worth reading before a price is agreed.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Grady County?
sections.html:
Population moved slowly for decades. Wikipedia's census table shows 18,457 people in 1910, 18,015 in 1960, 23,659 in 2000 and 25,011 in 2010. The county had 26,236 residents at the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate of 26,590 is a 1.4% increase. Roughly a fifth of residents (21.2%) are 65 or older, which makes age-based exemptions relevant for many owners planning a move.

sections.h2: Which Grady County offices handle valuation and billing?
sections.html:
Two offices divide the work. The commissioner's side covers bills for land, buildings, business property, vehicles, mobile homes and timber. The Tax Assessor office, headed by a chief appraiser, deals with returns, values and conservation or agricultural applications.

  • Tax commissioner, per the qPublic site: 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, property phone 229-377-3322, open Monday to Thursday from half past seven in the morning until six in the evening, shut on Fridays.
  • County service pages for the commissioner and the assessor: 33 17th Avenue NW, Cairo, GA 39827, with eight-to-five weekday hours.
  • Parcel lookup: the commissioner's qPublic site has a search tool covering each parcel.

Because the two pages show different addresses and hours, call 229-377-3322 before you travel and ask where to pay. Updates appear on the county's commissioner page and assessor page.

sections.h2: How does a Grady County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Georgia levies tax on 40% of a property's fair market value as of January 1, and a yearly notice lists both numbers. To challenge it, send a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice was mailed, choosing among the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator on state form PT-311A (Georgia Department of Revenue FAQ).

The 2024 cycle in Grady ran late. A delayed revaluation pushed assessment notices into September, and the county told owners that some appeal windows would end October 28 and others October 31. It added that the digest would reach the tax commissioner behind schedule, that the rate could not be set until December, and that commissioners expected a significant decrease in the mill rate after the revaluation (county notice).

File the notice and any appeal letter with your closing papers; the title company may want to know which value the bill is built on.

sections.h2: What due date will a Grady County bill show?
sections.html:
December 20 is the state's default deadline. According to the Department of Revenue's Grady facts page, local officials may pick December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments, so go by the date on your own bill. No interest runs for 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and penalties can be added to balances left unpaid (Grady County property tax facts).

For an overdue parcel, get penalty and interest figures from the commissioner. Three other fixed points apply here:

  • A return for property you held on January 1 is accepted from January 1 until April 1.
  • Mobile homes sitting in the county on January 1 must be returned for tax by April 1, at the same time as the location permit.
  • Anyone seeking a refund of wrongly assessed tax has three years from payment to start the claim.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments can Grady County owners claim?
sections.html:
A homestead application can go in at any point after you move in; April 1 is the final day for the first year. The assessor's page cites code section 48-5-44, and a missed filing counts as a waiver under state rules. The standard state deduction is $2,000 off assessed value. The Department's Grady facts page lists no local amounts on top of that, though it is dated 2016, so ask the assessor whether newer ones exist.

A county notice from January 2025 said the commissioners intended to opt out of the statewide adjusted base year homestead exemption and scheduled hearings for February 17 and 18, 2025. Check with the assessor on what that means for your home before telling a buyer the value is frozen.

  • Conservation use or preferential agricultural assessment: applications are accepted January 1 through April 1.
  • Freeport exemption on commercial and industrial inventory: available only where local voters adopted it, with filing on the return schedule.
  • A buyer files separately, since an exemption does not pass with the deed.

sections.h2: What did the county's 2026 millage notice say?
sections.html:
A county notice dated November 2026 said the Board of Commissioners had tentatively adopted a millage rate that raises property taxes by 4.72 percent. It printed a tentative rate of 12.64 mills, up .57 mill, compared with 12.070 mills at most without the increase, and listed three hearings that month at 33 17th Avenue NW in Cairo (county notice).

The figure speaks only to the county's own levy. School and city rates come separately, and final numbers show on the bill. For a payoff figure, request the adopted rates from the commissioner's office.

sections.h2: How should a Grady County seller handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
Liability for a year sits with the January 1 owner. By the Department of Revenue's account, selling on January 2 changes nothing, and no portion is refunded. Buyers and sellers therefore divide the bill in the contract and on the settlement statement, which should state who pays what.

  • Find out from the commissioner what the parcel owes for the present year and earlier ones.
  • Alert the closing agent to any open appeal, since a revised bill may follow.
  • Pass the payoff figure and the receiving office to the closing agent.
  • Tell the office once a homestead exemption stops applying because you have left.

A cash buyer taking the house as-is still receives the parcel along with its tax history, so arrears are best listed on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Grady County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Head to the tax commissioner's office in Cairo. The commissioner's own page gives 114 1st Street NE with Monday to Thursday hours, while the county service page gives 33 17th Avenue NW with weekday hours of eight to five. Call 229-377-3322 first to learn which counter takes payment.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Grady County value?
faqs.a: The limit is 45 days from the mailing date. Postmark your letter inside that period, address it to the Board of Tax Assessors on state form PT-311A, and name your route.

faqs.q: Does Grady County offer its own homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: The state's county facts page, dated 2016, shows only the statewide ones. Because of the county's 2025 opt-out notice, ask the assessor which freeze rules cover your home now.

faqs.q: If I close a Grady County sale in March, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner. No part of the year is refunded, so the contract and settlement statement set the split, and the commissioner can confirm the amount before you close.

faqs.q: Is a refund possible for Grady County tax paid in error?
faqs.a: Yes, if the tax was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected. Ask in writing within three years of paying. When the assessment is under appeal, the refund follows automatically once the final taxable value is fixed.
